title: A refused edit or undo records the refusal code in the ops signal, including the string error code the Claude Cowork engine sends
steps: S2: Call it with an answer that names no code, and with a code longer than 64 characters carrying control characters.
S3: Record site.edit and site.undo through createOpsSignal with a refusal field.
expect: S2: null; then the code without control characters, at most 64 characters.
S3: both rows keep refusal; site.edit still drops moment, site.undo keeps moment.

selectors.code: refusalCodeOf in apps/tracy-web/src/sites/refusal-code.js, used by applyDoor in apps/tracy-web/src/sites/route.js; FIELDS in apps/tracy-web/src/lib/ops-signal.js

evidence: Before this change every refused edit was recorded with refusal: null, because the engine sends error as a string and applyDoor read error.code
fence: The helper and the signal field filter without Postgres. Not exercised: a live engine answer through applyDoor.

tests: the code is read from each of the three refusal shapes
an answer that names no code is null
a code is bounded and carries no control characters
a refused edit and a refused undo both keep their code through the signal field filter
